title: Disaster Recovery Strategies
description: Compare backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, and multi-site active/active DR strategies.

data.text: **Disaster recovery (DR)** is the process of restoring your infrastructure after a major failure. AWS defines four common DR strategies, each offering different recovery times and costs.

data.title: DR Strategy Details
items: **Backup & Restore** — regular backups stored in S3; you rebuild the environment during recovery
**Pilot Light** — core components (database, networking) run in the DR region; app servers start on demand
**Warm Standby** — a scaled-down version of your full environment runs in the DR region; it can scale up quickly
**Multi-Site Active/Active** — traffic is distributed across regions with no single point of failure

data.text: A DR drill tests your recovery plan without actually disrupting production. AWS supports game days and simulated failures to validate that your RTO and RPO targets are achievable.

data.title: Remember
data.text: A DR plan is only useful if you test it regularly. Untested recovery plans often fail when you need them most.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Backup & Restore is cheapest but slowest to recover
Pilot Light keeps core infrastructure running for faster recovery
Warm Standby is nearly production-ready at all times
Active/Active provides the fastest recovery but at the highest cost
